prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1097; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The adjuster confirmed the policy was active and the reporting driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene confirm some details of the impact, including the position of both vehicles after the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward to the adjuster.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage to the rear of the insured's car matches the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 4: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The adjuster has requested the prior policy history to close this point.

Entry 5: The claimant, now represented by counsel, gave a recorded statement describing neck pain shortly after the impact. The account has been consistent with what the claimant told the adjuster in every earlier conversation.

Entry 6: It is not fully clear from the claimant's description or the photos where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting at the moment of impact. The adjuster has asked counsel for a seating diagram.

Entry 7: Medical records show a diagnosis of whiplash. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash, and the treating physician's causation opinion has been requested.

Entry 8: The records show no earlier injury to the same area of the neck or upper back. The adjuster has noted this for the file.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury, with physical therapy and medication. Visits tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 10: Counsel submitted a demand package with treatment bills and wage documentation. The adjuster is reviewing the bills against the records and the timeline of care.

Entry 11: File remains open pending the causation opinion and review of the demand. The adjuster will reassess reserves once those items are received.
